messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Types of CEL files?
parts:
Hi,
I am trying to download some data from Affy's website, and I have two
choices of types of CEL files and I don't know the difference nor
which is the appropriate one to use nor if it even matters. Here are
Affy's descriptions (these are exon arrays and I want to be able to
use Ken's cdf file for the analysis, if that helps...)
Thanks,
Elizabeth

GCOS Flat Files: This zip file contains XDA format CEL files and GCOS
XML files. These files are intended for use with Expression Console
and other Exon Array analysis software. They are not intended for
import into GCOS systems.

AGCC Flat Files: This zip file contains AGCC format CEL files and AGCC
ARR sample attribute files generated from the GCOS Flat Files. These
files are intended for use with Expression Console and other Exon
Array analysis software. They are not intended for import into GCOS
systems. The files were generated using a beta version of DEC
(software for converting files).

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Types of CEL files?
parts:

>
> Hi,
> I am trying to download some data from Affy's website, and I have two
> choices of types of CEL files and I don't know the difference nor
> which is the appropriate one to use nor if it even matters. Here are
> Affy's descriptions (these are exon arrays and I want to be able to
> use Ken's cdf file for the analysis, if that helps...)
> Thanks,
> Elizabeth
>
> GCOS Flat Files: This zip file contains XDA format CEL files and GCOS
> XML files. These files are intended for use with Expression Console
> and other Exon Array analysis software. They are not intended for
> import into GCOS systems.

The XDA CEL file format is the formal name for what we normally call
"binary" CEL files. See ?affxparser. See also Section "1.
Dictionary" in the HTML help of affxparser.

These files should do for you.

>
> AGCC Flat Files: This zip file contains AGCC format CEL files and AGCC
> ARR sample attribute files generated from the GCOS Flat Files. These
> files are intended for use with Expression Console and other Exon
> Array analysis software. They are not intended for import into GCOS
> systems. The files were generated using a beta version of DEC
> (software for converting files).

I do not know what "AGCC" stands for, but I know that "CC" have be
used for "Command Console files" which to the best of my knowledge is
also going under the work name "Calvin" files. Calvin is a new more
generic binary format from Affymetrix which is more flexible and more
generic, cf. XML. I'm not sure how well the standardized CEL files
are for this format; they are migrating towards using it (see e.g.
http://www.affymetrix.com/support/developer/apt_download/apt_changelog.affx),
but although affxparser should be able to read such CEL files out of
the box (it does on the few we tested), I would stick we the standard
binary files for now.

Hope this helps

Henrik
